newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-UNPREDICTABLE IRELAND EDGE OUT WALES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-UNPREDICTABLE IRELAND EDGE OUT WALES.

text.p: Ireland, the most unpredictable side in the Five Nations' championship, edged Wales 26-25 in yet another triumph at the national stadium on Saturday.
The fighting Irish have now won six times and drawn once in their last seven visits to the principality.

Wales, whose 34-19 win over Scotland in their opening match prompted speculation that a genuine Welsh revival is underway, got just the start they needed when Ieuan Evans scored in the opening minute.
The 32-year-old right wing danced through the defence after full-back Neil Jenkins had made a well-timed incursion into the line to extend his Welsh record for international tries to 32.
But Ireland stormed back with tries by Jonathan Bell, Eric Miller and debutant Dennis Hickie to take an ultimately decisive 20-10 lead at the interval.

Bell's try followed a high punt by fly-half Eric Elwood. Jenkins tried to take the ball under his posts but succeeded only in knocking it on to the padding around the uprights.Bell seized the rebound and dived over to score.
Number eight Miller burrowed over after a break by scrum-half Niall Hogan while right wing Hickie's try followed a break by recalled full-back Jim Staples carried on by flanker David Corkery.

Wales stormed back after the break and Evans was rewarded with his 33rd international try after their elusive little fly-half Arwel Thomas had ghosted through a gap following a quick tap penalty by his half-back partner Rob Howley.
But Ireland's defence, which disintegrated in the final quarter in the 32-15 loss to France a fortnight ago, held firm with the midfield backs putting in some heroic tackles.

Three minutes from time number eight Scott Quinnell revived Welsh hopes with a try converted by Jenkins but they could not get the extra points necessary to secure their second win of the championship.

Wales - 15-Neil Jenkins; 14-Ieuan Evans, 13-Gareth Thomas, 12-Scott Gibbs, 11-Dafydd James; 10-Arwel Thomas, 9-Rob Howley; 8-Scott Quinnell, 7-Colin Charvis (19-Kingsley Jones, 66)), 6-Steve Williams, 5-Mark Rowley (18-Craig Quinnell, 60), 4-Gareth Llewellyn, 3-David Young, 2-Jonathan Humphreys (captain), 1-Christian Loader.

Ireland - 15-Jim Staples (captain); 14-Dennis Hickie, 13-Jonathan Bell, 12-Maurice Field, 11-Dominic Crotty; 10-Eric Elwood, 9-Niall Hogan; 8-Eric Miller, 7-Denis McBride, 6-David Corkery, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Paddy Johns, 3-Paul Wallace, 2-Ross Nesdale, 1-Nick Popplewell.
